The US-Israel-Iran conflict is a blunt reminder that when India depends on imported crude, turmoil abroad can hit families at home. Workers and ordinary households feel higher fuel costs first, so cutting excise duties to ease the pressure is the right instinct—even if governments must manage the loss of revenue responsibly rather than simply passing the bill along later.

The deeper answer is national resilience: a dependable energy system that protects households from foreign shocks. We should put energy security and the interests of working families ahead of fashionable promises that leave the country exposed.
